about: ActiveOn Design Lab v2: the views and components to design, in exactly four groups (character, systems, time, map). Each component lists its purpose, where its data lives in data/v2/*.json (paths into that file; '*' every element, '[i]' or 'c<i>' one character), 2-4 variation ideas that change the UX, the brief.md principles it serves, the System Atlas entries it covers (numbers from research/system-atlas.md section 1), and whether the data comes with advice (adviceStatus). Data is scrubbed (Char1..., class + level only).
ownerFeedback: Builds must be taken into account and visualized; cards too; presets visualized and easy to understand per character, from cards we already have, plus a list of cards to grind for optimal presets, appropriate and possible for our world progress.
Dig deep into the game's other systems and flesh out their views and components.
Too linear, everything as cards, too simplified, not enough visuals, graphics and guidance; we don't get the insight to maximize game time efficiency and fun.
direction: Field Guide as the base; Quest Log accents for the why (NPC speech), headings at 16 px+ and celebrations; Command Board as the desktop and power-session layout (lanes, heat grids, ledgers). From critique.md.
hardConstraints: One who-glyph family: the class chibi at 16 px for every character reference; the map pin only for where.
Pixel faces only at 16 px and up; never for body text or anything under 12 px; no letter-spaced caps on pills.
44 px minimum tap targets; whole rows are the link.
Never repeat the row's own name in its action; never truncate the verb's object; group instead.
Exactly one NOW per plan, list, Walkthrough or picture.
Honest 'time not known' (or hide the token) instead of invented numbers; no '~' estimates on faces.
One currency format: coins with a short suffix.
No tier jargon and no field paths on screen.
No slot codes (C1..C6) on screen; characters are a chibi + class + level.
Our own pixel art only (ADR 0009); never embed or trace game sprites.

principles.P2: One next step, and it is the product
principles.P3: Who, where, how long, every line
principles.P7: One job, many characters: group it
principles.P8: Stable places; state by colour plus glyph plus word
principles.P11: The save is the checklist, and it is honest about age
principles.P12: Earned delight in our own pixel art

dataFiles.data/v2/*.lite.json: Same, trimmed for embedding (no expanded Now view, slimmer engine result and Account State). Paths in this inventory are into the lite files unless the field is missing there, then use the full file.

dataFiles.data/v2/kb-reference.json: Static Knowledge Base game data: maps, portals, world gates, class tree, tools, skill doors, card sets, statues, vault rows, death note tiers, construction and refinery facts
